nodes.label: Product Overview
nodes.rationale: Ater is designed as a technical blueprint for knowledge management, targeting power users and researchers with high-contrast, distraction-free monochrome aesthetic and progressive disclosure of complexity.

nodes.label: Ater Protocol Specification
nodes.rationale: Ater v33.0 outlines strict pedagogical rules for generating compact Obsidian atomic notes including mandatory YAML wikilinks formatting, continuous prose without bullet points, and an interactive quiz block to check comprehension.

nodes.label: Ater Core README
nodes.rationale: The primary monorepo physical mapping and physical boundaries of desktop, API sidecar, admin, and landing-page apps, explaining the offline-first Tauri v2 migration to native Rust and LanceDB.

nodes.label: Gemini Parsing Protocol
nodes.rationale: Defines monorepo ingest order and ignore directives for developer agents to prevent context amnesia and maximize token efficiency.

nodes.label: Ater Industrial Design Ground Truth
nodes.rationale: Specifies dark greyscale palette with 1px outline-variant divider rhythm, prohibiting white or light buttons in dark mode to preserve dark-room visual clarity.

nodes.label: Atomic Note: Java Technology
nodes.rationale: Pedagogical atomic note detailing Java's ecosystem (language, compiler, JRE, JVM, API) and the platform-dependency of the JVM to ensure cross-platform bytecode portability.

nodes.label: Atomic Note: Java Buzzwords
nodes.rationale: Captures Java's eight core design principles: Simple, Robust, Secured, Distributed, Multithreaded, Dynamic, Architecture-Neutral, and High Performance.

nodes.label: Atomic Note: Types Of Java Programs
nodes.rationale: Classifies Java applications into standalone, web, mobile, and enterprise structures, outlining their deployment and scaling patterns.
nodes.norm_label: atomic note: types of java programs

nodes.label: Atomic Note: Structured Programming
nodes.rationale: Details the procedural paradigm (functions, control structures, top-down design) and its limitations such as global variable side effects and hard-to-model domain changes.

nodes.label: Atomic Note: Object Oriented Programming
nodes.rationale: Explains the paradigm shift from functional procedures to data-and-object units (encapsulation) to reflect real-world actors, enhancing modularity and reusability.

nodes.label: Ater Admin Portal README
nodes.rationale: Describes Next.js admin app governing hardware activations, Supabase real-time waitlists, usage telemetry, and access DRM bindings.

nodes.label: Admin App Developer Rules
nodes.rationale: Enforces using local node_modules doc updates for Next.js to handle deprecations and breaking framework APIs.

nodes.label: Ater Desktop Client README
nodes.rationale: Architects Tauri v2 desktop application shell with LanceDB local vector RAG, local Obsidian vault browser, and Python FastAPI AI sidecar bridge.

nodes.label: System Prompt Template: Creator
nodes.rationale: Defines agent instructions to act as a co-creator generating high-quality options, writing, code snippet ideation, and slider-calibrated behavior refinement.

nodes.label: System Prompt Template: Strategist
nodes.rationale: Directs agent to function as an execution coach, tracking user personal/academic/financial/fitness goals, next actions, and accountability loops.

nodes.label: Ater Marketing Landing Page README
nodes.rationale: Public Next.js marketing and waitlist terminal styled in strict dark monochromatism with transparent client counts from Supabase.

nodes.label: Sidecar requirements.txt
nodes.rationale: Defines libraries (fastapi, google-genai, aiosqlite, sqlalchemy) powering Python API service layer.

nodes.label: Ater Sidecar README
nodes.rationale: FastAPI local sidecar coordinating Gemini LLM, TokenGovernor concurrent batch note compilation, SQLite caches, and Notion database syncer.

nodes.label: ONNX Model Vocabulary
nodes.rationale: Vocabulary file for local semantic token processing and RAG.

nodes.rationale: Original source document detailing programming paradigms, OOP principles, Java technology, editions, and compilation steps.

nodes.label: Java Virtual Machine
nodes.rationale: A platform-dependent runtime specification that executes platform-independent bytecode, realizing the 'Write Once, Run Anywhere' paradigm.

nodes.label: Java Runtime Environment
nodes.rationale: The physical implementation of the JVM that packages core libraries and supporting files to run compiled Java apps.

nodes.label: Java Application Programming Interface
nodes.rationale: A large collection of pre-written software packages that insulate application code from the details of the underlying system hardware.

nodes.label: Java Bytecode
nodes.rationale: Intermediate machine-independent representation of compiled Java source code, generated by javac and executed by the JVM.

nodes.label: Automatic Memory Management
nodes.rationale: The JVM mechanism that automatically manages memory allocation and deallocation for objects, reducing memory leak hazards but potentially introducing timing spikes.

nodes.label: Architecture-Neutral Principle
nodes.rationale: Core Java buzzword ensuring bytecode runs unmodified on any hardware target containing a standard JVM.

nodes.label: Robustness Principle
nodes.rationale: Java principle emphasizing compile-time static type-checking, structured runtime exception handling, and elimination of direct pointer address modifications to guarantee system stability.

nodes.label: Secured Principle
nodes.rationale: Ensured through a multi-tier sandbox model including bytecode verifier, security managers, and restricted execution environments.

nodes.label: Programming Paradigms
nodes.rationale: High-level categorization of programming models and execution philosophies (e.g. Unstructured, Structured, Object-Oriented).

nodes.label: Structured Programming Paradigm
nodes.rationale: A top-down functional paradigm using local variable boundaries, custom procedures, and control structures (if-else/loops) to enhance procedural readability.

nodes.label: Object-Oriented Programming Paradigm
nodes.rationale: A modular blueprint-based paradigm combining data and behaviors into class-instantiated object boundaries to accurately model real-world actors.

nodes.label: Encapsulation
nodes.rationale: Hiding internal state variables (private) and restricting access through public methods (getters/setters) to preserve state integrity and shield variables from corruption.

nodes.label: Abstraction
nodes.rationale: Exposing essential signatures and hiding concrete implementation details using interfaces and abstract classes to simplify client interactions.

nodes.label: Inheritance
nodes.rationale: Establishing parent-child relationships (IS-A) allowing subclasses to reuse superclass attributes/methods and override behaviors.

nodes.label: Polymorphism
nodes.rationale: Enabling one interface to represent multiple dynamic forms, achieved via compile-time overloading and runtime dynamic method overriding.

nodes.label: Class blueprint
nodes.rationale: Logical template containing instance and static variables and methods, consuming no memory until instantiated.

nodes.label: Object instance
nodes.rationale: A concrete entity possessing unique state, behavior, and distinct identity created in heap memory.

nodes.label: Constructor
nodes.rationale: A special class method with no return type, used to initialize object variables, which can be overloaded or cascaded.

nodes.label: this Keyword reference
nodes.rationale: References the current object context inside methods or constructors, commonly used to resolve namespace shadowing or trigger cascading constructors.

nodes.label: static Keyword modifier
nodes.rationale: Creates class-level variables/methods shared across all instances, which can be accessed without creating any objects, but cannot access non-static instance fields.

nodes.label: Package Namespace
nodes.rationale: A namespace structure for containing a group of related classes to prevent naming collisions and manage visibility.

nodes.label: Standalone Applications
nodes.rationale: Desktop CLI or GUI based standalone applications executed locally on the host operating system.

nodes.label: Web Applications
nodes.rationale: Server-side Java components executing JSP, Servlets, or Spring Boot generating dynamic web content via HTTP.

nodes.label: Mobile Applications
nodes.rationale: Mobile platforms developed utilizing Java ME or Android platform architectures.

nodes.label: Enterprise Applications
nodes.rationale: Large-scale distributed architectures built utilizing Jakarta EE, EJB, JMS, and JPA structures.
